text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Australian Taxation Office yesterday handed the Adsteam group (formerly the Adelaide Steamship Co) a massive tax bill approaching A$1 billion. The revised tax assessment of $975 million consisting of back taxes for the financial years 1990-91, 1991-2 and 1992-93 includes A$443.82 million in interest and penalties. Page 21

Amcor restructuring of Paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd has led to a comprehensive review of its pulp and paper operations. An initial part of the shake-up is yesterday's closure of its Broadford board mill in Victoria after 107 years of operation. Page 21.

Sydney-based gold company Goldfields Ltd has announced that production for the June quarter had increased to 131,234 ounces compared with 129,485 ounces for the same period last year. This outcome was achieved despite a fall in output at its 24 per cent wned Porgera mine in Papua New Guinea. Page 22.

Anaconda Nickel Ltd has successfully completed its attempt to fund its Murrin Murrin nickel and cobalt mine in Western Australia. The company has raised A$96.4 million from the placement of 25 million shares to major local and overseas institutions at anaverage price of A$3.85. Page 22.

Australia's biggest regional carrier, Kendell Airlines, has urged the New South Wales Government to proceed with interstate deregulation plans claiming it will result in lower fares. Kendall Airlines chairman Don Kendall yesterday recommended the New Souh Wales Government adopts the recommendations recently released by the Independent Pricing and Regulatory Tribunal to fully deregulate interstate air travel from 1999. Page 22.

Brierley Investments Ltd chief executive Paul Collins has been recorded as saying the company is not currently considering any plans to rid itself of its 42.5 per cent stake in Air New Zealand. Speculation has arisen recently over Brierley Investment's cmmitment to its holding following the expected drop in the airline's earnings for the 1996-97 year and the interest shown by Singapore Airlines in acquiring an interest. Page 24.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Independent Wholesalers has established a new national independent banner, Food-Works Supermarket Group, which hopes to open 150 stores and achieve sales of A$350 million in its first year of operation. The move is a serious threat to the Davids' monopoly on independent supermarkets. Page 23.

The Australian Stock Exchange yesterday suspended Aristocrat Leisure Industries from trading following accusations of "unsuitable business practices and association" by gaming authorities in the United States. The company was recently awarded a contract by the New South Wales Casino Control Authority to supply poker machines to the Sydney Harbour Casino. Page 23.

TNT managing director David Mortimer and chairman of the Mortimer review of industry programs said yesterday the A$1 billion five-year Invest Australia program recommended by the review should be allocated to many small-scale projects. The review says th fund is necessary in order to improve investment opportunities in Australia relative to other countries. Page 25. --

Australian company Rio Tinto has approved a two-year feasibility study into its A$540 million Las Cruces high-grade copper deposit in Spain. The company said yesterday it would pursue analysis of the drilling, environmental, mining and economic aspects of the project with a hope to further development. Page 25.

Woodside Petroleum, the project operator of the North West Shelf natural gas project off the West Australian coast, confirmed yesterday it had signed a contract to supply the State Government utility, AlintaGas. The 15-year contract is believed to be worth A$1 billion and will see Woodside Petroleum supplying up to 80 terrajoules of gas per day. Page 26.

Australian company Grenfell Resources confirmed yesterday that a two-year clearance access agreement had been negotiated with Aboriginal communities in South Australia's Gawler Craton region. Grenfell Resources director Nick Limb said the agreement was amodel for successful negotiations between Aboriginal groups and mining companies. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Economists' forecasts that inflation would remain low until at least the end of the year, and an indication from United States Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan that a rise in US rates was some way off, yesterday increased the likelihood of a cut to home and business lending rates. Page 31.

Westpac Banking Corporation is confident its cash reserves will remain strong after it beds down the A$1.4 billion bid for the Bank of Melbourne, and has abandoned plans for a A$500 million converting preference share issue. Westpac chief financial office Pat Handley said it would not be acceptable to shareholders for the bank to raise more funds when it wasn't necessary. Page 31.

First State Fund Managers and Mercantile Mutual Funds Management, who hold 13 per cent and 5 per cent stakes in Hawker Richardson respectively have rejected Austrim's A$1.86 per share takeover offer as too low. Rothschild Australia, a 15.6 per cent stakeholder had earlier rejected an offer for the same reason. Austrim chairman Alan Jackson will hold meetings with the investors in Sydney today. Page 33.

Federal Court Justice Graham Hill said yesterday that Canadian media group CanWest Global Communications would win the dispute with the Australian Broadcasting Authority over the Ten Group if a strict legal definition of "control" was applied, but not if a broader definition was used. Hill reserved his judgment yesterday and is expected to hand down his ruling in about one month. Page 33.

Macquarie Bank has experienced bumper first quarter earnings due to the booming share, commodity and bond markets, setting the bank up for another record profit. Macquarie confirmed yesterday it considering reducing its high level of capital through techniques such as a buyback. Page 33.

Kerry Stokes' Seven Network has joined the Baulderstone Hornibrook consortium's bid for the Docklands Stadium in Melbourne, in an attempt to win the broadcast rights of the Australian Football League. The move is considered a defensive response to the decsion by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting to join rival bidder, the Transfield/Grocoa consortium, and his ties with third bidder Hudson Conway/Lend Lease. Page 31.
THE AGE

The release yesterday of inflation figures which record Australia's first negative quarter for the consumer price index since 1992 and place the annual inflation rate at below 2 per cent has increased speculation of a fifth consecutive cut in official intrest rates. Citibank chief economist Stephen Koukoulas said yesterday that the Reserve Bank of Australia would act soon to cut interest rates in order to link the move to the good economic news. Page B1.

Sydney-based entertainment group Hoyts Cinemas yesterday offered a one-for-six renounceable rights issue to raise A$95 million, to help capitalise on expansion opportunities in Latin America and Europe. It is the third time in a year the group has gone tothe sharemarket to raise capital, and brings the total raised since August to A$250 million. Page B3.

A series of exploration successes by Cultus Petroleum has fuelled speculation of a takeover, with the most likely predator being Shell Oil, one of its partners in the big Cornea discovery in the Browse Basin off northern Australia. Most analysts believe te Cornea partnership would be more workable if 25 per cent stakeholder Cultus was taken out, leaving just Shell and US Chevron. Page B1.

Macquarie Bank confirmed at its annual general meeting yesterday it is considering reducing its high levels of capital. Credit rating agencies are comfortable with a drop in the tier-one capital adequacy ratio from 13 per cent to 9 per cent, worth about A150 million, but Macquarie managing director Allan Moss said any reduction in capital was likely to be modest. Page B2

Industry chiefs including Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries chief executive Ian Grigg and Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry chief executive Mark Paterson last night praised the Mortimer review of business programs for highlighting economi growth, research and development, investment, export development and tax reform. The review is seen as a blueprint for the Federal Government's approach to industry assistance. Page B3.

Austrim representatives will meet with First State Fund Management, Mercantile Mutual Funds Management and Rothschild Australia Asset Management who have all rejected the company's A$1.68 a share bid for their stakes in Hawker Richardson. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
